title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' (sequel to La Longue Marche). An element of the Galois/GT-type group is given by data (μ, f), with μ ∈ Ẑ* (the cyclotomic character) and f in π̂_{0,3}. Grothendieck follows its action through the homomorphism N_{1,1} → GL(2,Ẑ) (§39) on the level-one 'genus 1' quotient.

The matrices in play:
- ρ = [[0,1],[-1,1]], of order 6 with ρ^3 = -1 (the order-3 symmetry of P^1∖{0,1,∞}).
- σ_∞ = [[0,1],[-1,0]], of order 4.
- From the previous page: g = (1+μt(t+u), -μt^2; -1+μu(t+u), 1-μut), a twisted cocycle with g ρ(g) ρ^2(g) = ε_2, and ε_2 g = α ρ(α)^{-1}.

The problem. Find u ∈ GL(2,Ẑ) with det u = μ which induces, by inner automorphism on SL(2,Ẑ)', the same automorphism as the original one. Explicitly:
- (66) det u = μ;
- (67) u σ_∞ u^{-1} = ε' σ_∞;
- (68) u ρ u^{-1} = ε'' g ρ, with ε', ε'' ∈ {±1}.

Step 1 (sign ε''). Write ρ(x) = ρxρ^{-1}. Then (68) reads u ρ(u)^{-1} = ε'' g. Apply the 'norm' N(x) = x ρ(x) ρ^2(x).
- For a coboundary x = u ρ(u)^{-1}, the product telescopes to u ρ^3(u)^{-1} = 1, because ρ^3 = -1 is central.
- On the other side, N(ε'' g) = ε''^3 N(g) = ε'' ε_2.
- Hence ε'' = ε_2 (68 bis).

Step 2 (Hilbert-90-type reduction). Now u ρ(u)^{-1} = α ρ(α)^{-1}. So u_0 := α^{-1} u commutes with ρ, and u = α u_0 (69).

Step 3 (indeterminacy). Since σ_∞ and ρ topologically generate SL(2,Ẑ), (67) and (68) fix u only up to a scalar λ ∈ Ẑ*. Condition (66) then forces λ^2 = 1, i.e. λ ∈ ₂Ẑ* ≅ {±1}^P. Grothendieck hopes to find a canonical choice nonetheless.

Step 4 (earlier route). In his first computations, the commutant of ρ was written as u_0 = p + qρ = (p, q; -q, p+q), i.e. an element of Ẑ[ζ_6]. Hence (next page):
- det u_0 = p^2 + pq + q^2 = μ ε_3;
- combined with (67), this led to u_0 = μ(cρ + d), in the case ε' = +1 only.

Final result (next page, (74)). u = μ(t σ_∞ + u) = μ(u, t; -t, u), expressed directly in the abelianized entries of f. This u commutes with σ_∞, i.e. it lies in the Gaussian Cartan Ẑ[i]. Grothendieck suspects that ε' = +1 iff p ≡ 1 mod 4, from compatibility with class field theory.

What this serves. Essentially, he extracts from the action on π̂_{0,3} a canonical lift in GL(2,Ẑ) of the outer Galois action on SL(2,Ẑ)'. This amounts to the Tate-module action for the CM situations with automorphism groups of order 6 and 4 (j = 0, j = 1728), written explicitly in terms of (μ, f).
errors: No genuine errors on this page; the telescoping argument is correct given ρ^3 = -1 central and ε'' scalar.

Uniqueness modulo scalars is correct but tacit. A u' differing by v with v ∈ Ẑ[ρ]* and v σ_∞ v^{-1} = -σ_∞ would require v proportional to √-3 = 2ρ-1, which is not a unit at 3. So only scalars remain, and with (66) only λ^2 = 1.
The notation clash (u for the matrix and u for an entry of f) is noted by Grothendieck himself on the next page.

ideas.what: Using the norm map x ↦ xρ(x)ρ^2(x) (a Z/3 twisted-cocycle norm) to pin down the sign ε'' = ε_2
ideas.modern_name: Norm of a 1-cocycle for a cyclic group / triviality of norms of coboundaries

ideas.what: Reducing u to α·u_0 with u_0 in the commutant of ρ, i.e. in Ẑ[ζ_6] (Eisenstein Cartan); norm form p^2+pq+q^2
ideas.modern_name: Hilbert 90-type splitting; non-split Cartan / CM by Z[ζ_3]

ideas.what: Canonical lift u ∈ GL(2,Ẑ), det u = μ, of the outer action of a (μ,f) automorphism on SL(2,Ẑ)', ambiguous only up to {±1}^P; final formula u = μ(tσ_∞+u) in terms of abelianized f
ideas.modern_name: Linear (congruence/abelian) part of the GT / Galois action on Γ̂_{1,1}; Tate module of CM elliptic curves from π_1(P^1∖{0,1,∞})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (Annals 1986, CM and braid groups), Anderson, Coleman; Nakamura, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura–Schneps for GT and genus 1

missed.claim: Grothendieck seeks a canonical choice of the sign ambiguity in {±1}^P for the GL(2,Ẑ)-lift, and conjectures (next page) that ε' = +1 iff p ≡ 1 mod 4. This is a class-field-theoretic sign law for the explicit lift written in terms of f.
missed.quote: u est déterminé seulement modulo λ satisfaisant λ^2=1 i.e. modulo ₂Ẑ*≃{±1}^P ..., mais on espère néanmoins tomber sur un choix canonique.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an explicit formula linking the abelianized Drinfeld/Ihara element f to Hecke characters of Q(i) and Q(ζ_3). It parallels Ihara–Anderson–Coleman Jacobi-sum formulas, but in the SL(2)/genus-1 setting. The exact form and sign normalization may not appear in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but largely routine cohomological computation in a long calculation. The underlying link (Galois action on π_1 of P^1∖{0,1,∞} versus CM Galois representations) is known through Ihara, Anderson, Coleman and Nakamura. Only the explicit normalized formula and the sign question are mildly novel details.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: the insertion reads 'que le u initial (par passage aux quotients)'; 'le initial' is inserted above 'u'.
The equation label at the bottom left looks like '(70)' (possibly written as '(79)'); '153' at the bottom left is the archive page number.
In (70) the matrix is (p, q; -q, p+q); the stray '1' after p is the identity matrix (u_0 = p·1 + qρ).
